meta.description: Reference guides for pallet buyers: grades, sizes, heat treatment, load capacity, pricing, and freight, written from a pallet brokerage desk.

hero.heading: Pallet Resource Library
hero.directAnswer: The AGL Pallet Resource Library is a reference set for buyers who spec, source, and ship on pallets. Each guide opens with a short answer, then works through grades, sizes, heat treatment, load capacity, pricing, freight, and standards, and the calculators turn a few inputs into planning estimates. For anything the guides leave open, our brokerage desk answers spec questions directly.

pillars.title: GMA Pallets and Grades
pillars.directAnswer: A GMA pallet is a 48 × 40 inch (1219 × 1016 mm) wood stringer pallet used across North American grocery and consumer-goods shipping. The name describes a footprint and a construction style, not a single blueprint. Pallet grades such as A, B, and C are trade labels, not a published standard, so confirm the acceptance criteria in writing.

pillars.title: Heat-Treated Pallets and ISPM-15
pillars.directAnswer: ISPM-15 is the international rule for wood packaging that crosses a border. Heat treatment, the method most North American export pallets use, means the wood is heated to at least 56 °C at the wood core for 30 continuous minutes, then marked with a bordered stamp. Domestic shipments that stay inside the United States do not require it.

pillars.title: Pallet Glossary
pillars.directAnswer: The pallet glossary defines the terms buyers meet when specifying and shipping on pallets, from deckboards, stringers, and blocks to entry types, grades, and treatment marks. Plain definitions make it easier to write a clear spec, compare quotes on equal terms, and talk through requirements with suppliers and carriers.

pillars.title: Pallet Weight and Load Capacity
pillars.directAnswer: Published figures for a 48 × 40 wood stringer pallet commonly run about 33–48 lb, and a figure near 37 lb is often cited for a typical build. Species, moisture, and board count move the number. Load capacity depends on support: static on the floor, dynamic on a forklift, or racked on beams.

pillars.title: Pallet Sizes
pillars.directAnswer: Pallet sizes are set by the product, the trailer, and the receiving customer rather than by one universal standard. North American buyers most often see the GMA footprint, while other industries and export lanes use their own dimensions. Matching pallet size to the load and the truck keeps freight costs predictable.

pillars.title: Skid vs. Pallet
pillars.directAnswer: A skid is a platform with runners and no bottom deck, while a pallet typically adds a bottom deck. Skids are simpler and often used for heavy or stationary loads; pallets add stability and forklift entry options for racking and stacking. The terms are often used interchangeably in everyday shipping.

pillars.title: Pallet Prices
pillars.directAnswer: Pallet prices move with lumber markets, freight, order volume, and specification. New stock pallets, custom sizes, and heat-treated builds each price differently, and delivered cost often matters more than the unit price. A quote built on a clear spec, quantity, and delivery location is the most reliable way to compare options.

pillars.title: Pallets per Truckload
pillars.directAnswer: For 48 × 40 pallets, a 53 ft dry van takes 26 pallets loaded straight or 30 turned, single-stacked. Empty 48 × 40 wood pallets about 6 in tall and 37 lb come to roughly 510 on that van when turned: 30 stacks of 17. Weight limits and receiver rules can cut a loaded count before the floor is full.

pillars.title: Pallet Calculators
pillars.directAnswer: Pallet calculators turn a few inputs, such as footprint, load weight, and trailer size, into planning estimates for loads per truck, pallet counts, and freight needs. Estimates are a starting point, not a spec. Real-world results depend on product dimensions, stacking limits, and the receiving customer's requirements.

pillars.title: Types of Pallets
pillars.directAnswer: Wood pallets come in two main construction types: stringer pallets, which rest on lengthwise support boards and are common for domestic shipping, and block pallets, which use blocks for true four-way forklift entry. Beyond construction, pallets differ by deck coverage, wood species, treatment, and whether they are standard sizes or custom builds.

pillars.title: Pooled vs. Owned Pallets
pillars.directAnswer: Pooled pallets are rented from a pallet pool and returned through the pool's network, while owned pallets are purchased outright and stay with the buyer or move one way with the product. The right choice depends on shipping lanes, return logistics, customer requirements, and how much administrative tracking a team can support.

pillars.title: Pallet Standards
pillars.directAnswer: Pallet standards are published specifications that define dimensions, construction, testing methods, and treatment for wood packaging. They come from industry associations, standards bodies, and international agreements, and large receivers often add their own requirements. Knowing which standard applies to a lane or customer keeps loads from being rejected at the dock.
